jobs.prompt: Write docs/architecture/swarm-v2.md (new file) and extend docs/scope/roadmap.md. The document is an architecture proposal of 1 to 2 pages (about 100 to 130 lines), plain short sentences, for the owner to review; it builds nothing. Structure: a short Goal paragraph; then for EACH of the 8 target-design items a short section with four labeled lines: Today (what exists now), Gap, Effort (S, M or L with one clause why), Migration (steps that never break a running project: how old and new run side by side, what is flagged, what is the fallback). The 8 items: (1) a per-machine swarm service under launchd with sessions becoming clients of it; (2) one chief orchestrator across all projects; (3) swarm state outside the repo so repos stay clean (state directory per project under a machine data folder, repo keeps only the pointer and the scope and tickets that are meant to be committed); (4) per-job isolation (container or worktree with its own database and ports) and enforced permissions (file, network and git permissions granted per job by the service) instead of a text guard; (5) a multi-machine cluster with one queue and one board; (6) cloud burst runners; (7) one-command install plus swarm doctor plus swarm add REPO; (8) one event store in SQLite replacing the scattered ndjson and markdown ledgers (events table, views for the board, exports for the repo). End with a short Suggested order (what to do first and why, with the dependencies between items, for example the event store before the service, state outside the repo before multi-machine) and a short Risks line. Facts about today (use them, do not invent): Swarm runs as short-lived commands, one process per run; there is no per-machine daemon except swarm watch and swarm remote serve (board), and a per-project autopilot loop; swarm orchestrator up (#206) starts one tmux session per project running claude remote-control, with a launchd agent at login. State lives in each repo's .swarm folder (gitignored: runs, tickets ledger, journal ndjson, orchestrator events, handbuild guard state) plus per-machine files under the home .project-swarm folder (the install, the spend store, the live-run registry, busy markers) and the machine config under .config/project-swarm. The usage ledger and HANDOFF are generated markdown files inside the repo. The board (Swarm Watch) reads those files. Multi-machine today: a swarm-inbox git repo and the field export and collect modules over git; the Mac mini runs its own clone and its own sessions; there is no shared queue. Per-job isolation today: a copied workspace per job with a sandbox profile, scratch worktrees for integration, Cursor and Codex lanes see committed HEAD only (an integrated snapshot module exists on a branch); jobs share the machine's ports and databases. Permissions today: a text-level hand-build guard hook on the orchestrator's tool calls (honest-but-fallible threat model), git pre-commit and pre-push hooks, and GitHub branch protection on main. Cloud: a rented GPU lane (vast and lambda style) exists; no general cloud runners. Install today: node tools/install.mjs --user and swarm update from tags, swarm doctor checks lanes, swarm init links a project; there is no swarm add. Events today: ndjson files and markdown ledgers in several places, with the board assembling views from them. Then edit docs/scope/roadmap.md: add stage S7 Swarm v2 architecture to the Stages list, and add a section ## S7 Swarm v2 architecture at the end with requirements R-040 to R-047, one per item, using exactly the file's existing format: a heading line ### R-0NN followed by a one-sentence title that states the outcome, then Acceptance: and 2 or 3 measurable bullet lines each (numbers, commands and outcomes that can be checked, no vague words like clean or robust). Examples of measurable acceptance: swarm service start survives a reboot and a client reconnects within 5 seconds; a repo has no .swarm folder after a full wave and git status is clean; two jobs run at the same time with different ports and databases and neither sees the other; the same ticket ledger is visible from both machines with one queue; swarm add REPO registers a project and shows it on the board in under 60 seconds; the event store answers the board's views with the same numbers as today's ledgers on a sample project. Keep the existing text of the roadmap unchanged except for the Stages list and the new section, and keep the Version line. Make sure the roadmap still parses: it must keep 39 existing requirements plus 8 new ones (47) and stages S1 to S7. Write only docs/architecture/swarm-v2.md and docs/scope/roadmap.md.
